first_impression.reaction: Typed 'santorini or mykonos wedding' on the train. The first paragraph already tells me the difference: cliff and caldera versus beaches and town. Takeaways are short. I'd swipe the table, jump to the 'which island suits you' bit and the FAQ, then bookmark it.

journey.quote: Santorini is the caldera: cliff-top villages along the rim of a volcano, with ceremonies that face the water and the sunset.
journey.reaction: That's the difference in one line, and the Mykonos line right after it matches. Exactly what I searched for.

journey.section: Santorini or Mykonos for your wedding: the short answer
journey.quote: If the picture is bare feet near the sea, a chapel above a beach and a town to wander into after dinner, that is Mykonos.
journey.reaction: No winner, fine, but this makes it easy to pick for myself. I can see which one I am in two sentences.

journey.quote: The Australian paperwork is the same whichever island you choose, starting with proof that neither of you is already married, such as a Certificate of No Impediment.
journey.reaction: Australian paperwork in the takeaways. I'm in Singapore, so one of my four quick bullets isn't for me. Still, I get the idea that the island doesn't change the papers.

journey.section: Santorini vs Mykonos at a glance
journey.quote: Same figures for both: HNMS Naxos, the nearest listed station
journey.reaction: In a quick table this reads like code. What is HNMS? Why Naxos when I asked about Santorini and Mykonos? I had to scroll way down to work out it just means the weather is the same for both.

journey.section: Santorini vs Mykonos at a glance
journey.reaction: Only two columns, so it fits on my phone without swiping. Good.

journey.section: Setting and feel: caldera cliff tops or beaches and Mykonos Town
journey.quote: That matters more than it sounds: it is why a winery is one of Santorini's wedding venues.
journey.reaction: Didn't know you could marry at a winery there. Nice detail.

journey.section: Setting and feel: caldera cliff tops or beaches and Mykonos Town
journey.quote: Hamlets spread across the rim of the caldera, so most ceremony spaces look west and down, over water, to the volcanic islands.
journey.reaction: By now I've read caldera rim, cliffs and sunset in the intro, the short answer, the takeaways and the table. Same point again, more scrolling.

journey.quote: Mykonos Grand states that both partners must be Christian Orthodox for a religious wedding on the hotel premises.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of thing nobody tells you until it's too late. Real, specific, useful. Bookmark-worthy.

journey.quote: The Myconian Collection has certified halal and kosher kitchens and a South Asian chef for traditional Indian cuisine.
journey.reaction: Okay, this one I'd screenshot. Half my guest list would care about this.

journey.quote: The airlines serving Santorini Airport include Aegean Airlines, Olympic Air and Sky Express, alongside European and Gulf carriers such as British Airways, Lufthansa, Qatar Airways, Etihad Airways, Gulf Air and FlyDubai.
journey.reaction: Long airline list on a phone. I skimmed past it. The ferry and wind warning below is the bit that actually matters.

journey.section: When to marry on each island
journey.quote: Smartraveller also notes that Greece sits in an active seismic zone, with earthquakes and volcanic activity near major destinations including Santorini, and advises following local authorities.
journey.reaction: Slightly scary, but I'd rather know. Makes the page feel honest and current.

journey.quote: **You want a beach-side weekend.** Mykonos. Its wedding hotels sit on Ornos, Psarou, Agios Ioannis and Elia, so the beach is part of the venue rather than a day trip.
journey.reaction: This whole section is the real answer to my search, in bold one-liners. But it's near the bottom, after the weather and the legal stuff. I nearly didn't get here.

journey.section: Santorini or Mykonos wedding questions, answered
journey.quote: The island matters less than the choices you make on it.
journey.reaction: Just tell me how much it costs. I get that it depends, and it does say what it depends on, but I still don't know if one is pricier.

journey.section: Choose your island with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: So it's mainly for Australians. Not sure it's for me.

unanswered_questions: Is a wedding on one island usually pricier than the other? Even a rough sense would help.
Do you work with couples who aren't Australian?
What does 'HNMS' stand for, without having to scroll down to find out?
